I reproduced the original failure on 6c61f2e: QA13-V5 (meta.cwd and the deny list forged to /somewhere/else while the transcript says /work/repo) gives validateGate [] there. On 1e64eb0 that old fixture is rejected, but only partly for the right reason: it has no init cwd at all (08-r13-suite-old-vs-new.log). So my independent round-14 cases use a fixture whose init line carries cwd, like real transcripts. All 18 pass on 1e64eb0, and 9 fail on 6c61f2e (09-qa14-new-cases.log). QA14-V12 is the exact original forgery (meta.cwd and deny list set to /somewhere/else, init and prompt at /work/repo). It returns [] on 6c61f2e. On 1e64eb0 it is rejected by both the init check and the prompt check, and only for the forged run. V2 to V5 also fail on 6c61f2e: V2 (init without cwd), V3 (meta and init forged consistently, only the prompt still says /work/repo, rejected by the prompt check alone), V4 (prompt with no working-directory sentence) and V5 (trailing-slash meta.cwd, strict). Positive controls V1, V8, V9 and V10 bind: spaces, parentheses, Arabic, and absolute Write paths under a consistent cwd. The round-9 suite still passes 91 of 94. The 3 others are one-field-only cwd fixtures (QA7-N77, QA8-F223, QA9-C01), and they now fail only with cwd-binding errors, as they should. Every one of the 63 real recorded runs has init cwd equal to meta.cwd, and so do all 26 runs with a string replayed prompt. The existing candidate test 'F-DG0-233: meta.cwd is bound to the transcript' passes. Limits I recorded, not findings: a whole-evidence consistent forgery (V6), and an extra resume init line naming another cwd (V7, only the first init is compared), are still accepted. Both need fabricated self-hashed run evidence, which is disclosed residual 1. The runner uses one $CWD for every attempt (run-agent.sh lines 150 and 159), so it cannot produce either.
